headline: The stall machine: RL learns to farm kills and lose the team
lede: Stage 3b shipped in retrogames-rl (PR #4, main@5bff4c5): goal files plus an evolution-strategies trainer fine-tune the BC partner against the real Gauntlet sim on named goals. The first two trained goals landed the plan's two predicted failure modes on the same day — progress saturated its validation signal yet generalized to nothing, and hunter confirmed the stall: 108 partner kills on held-out, 22k ticks, wins halved.

notes.text: #2515 closed shipped: goals/*.js (9 hypotheses over canonical signals) + train-goal.mjs — deterministic antithetic ES, seed discipline enforced in code, checkpoint pick on validation only, held-out ONCE per model via a sha registry. progress-rl-v1 val 0.9875->1.0000, held-out 0.9833 (== v4: the gain was one fractional level, not skill).

hunter-rl-v1: objective 1.8 with 3/6 wins, 18 hero deaths, idle-level pace — exactly the stage-3 plan's committed prediction that optimizing kills teaches stalling. The Plaicraft question is now measurable: same signals, different weights, wildly different partners.

Two honest ledger notes: a warden-killed session's ES trainers survived as orphans and were resumed mid-flight (progress 15/20), and progress's held-out ran through the studio remote-control line on byte-identical weights — the once-registry refused the duplicate, and both provenances are recorded on the issue.
